Region: The Negev and the southern wilderness, associated with Midian and with Judah's southern border
History: The Kenites are named in the land promise of Genesis 15:19 and in Balaam's oracle, which pictures their nest set in the rock (Numbers 24:21). The children of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up with Judah into the wilderness of Judah (Judges 1:16), and Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites when his wife Jael killed Sisera (Judges 4:11, 17-22). Saul warned the Kenites to leave the Amalekites before his campaign, because they had shown kindness to Israel coming out of Egypt (1 Samuel 15:6). David shared spoil with the Kenites (1 Samuel 30:29), and 1 Chronicles 2:55 counts scribal families among the Kenites, including the house of Rechab, whose abstinent rule Jeremiah 35 praises.
Culture: The name is traditionally connected with metalworking (Hebrew qayin, 'smith'), and the Kenites lived as tent-dwellers on the desert fringe, at home among both Midian and Judah. The Rechabites kept Jonadab's rule: no wine, no houses, no sown fields.
Religion: Jethro's family acknowledged the LORD (Exodus 18), and the Rechabites' obedience to their ancestor's command is held up in Jeremiah 35 as a rebuke to Judah's disobedience.
BibleConnection: Kenites are Israel's desert friends: kin by marriage to Moses, allies who showed kindness at the exodus, and the people whose tent Jael's peg ended Sisera's army.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 15:19; Numbers 24:21; Judges 1:16; Judges 4:11; Judges 4:17-22; 1 Samuel 15:6; 1 Chronicles 2:55; Jeremiah 35:6-10
